Jordan — high level from finance:

1) Net terms: Finance prefers Net30 by default. We can consider Net45 for strategic accounts but require either (a) an approved credit check + signed PO up front, or (b) payment via ACH for the first invoice to mitigate risk. If Acme provides a signed PO and (ideally) a PO number on the DocuSign envelope, finance is comfortable approving Net45.

2) Billing entity: We can invoice to Acme US, Inc. but the counterparty on the MSA must align or we must include a billing clause in the Order Form stating: "For invoicing purposes only, Customer billing entity is Acme US, Inc.; payments shall be sent to Redwood Inference XX bank account unless otherwise agreed in writing." We will need Acme's tax ID/EIN and W-9/W-8 equivalents for their entity to set up the account.

3) Tax certificates: If Acme expects Redwood to not gross up for withholdings, we require tax residency / certificate documentation before invoicing. Please ask Acme to send their tax certs (they mentioned this). I attached a short checklist for what Finance needs to process invoices.

Next steps I recommend: request from Acme — (A) copy of signed PO with PO number, (B) billing entity EIN + tax certificate, (C) AP email for invoice routing (we usually use ap@acme.com). If they can provide those by EOD Wed we can approve Net45 and route invoices accordingly.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: ACME_Tax_Certificates_Request.docx

Jordan / Lauren — legal comments below and suggested playbook. I reviewed Acme's redlines and Jordan's proposed response. High-level: we can accept an alternate invoicing entity, but we need contract language to make it explicit and to protect Redwood on tax / indemnity.

Suggested clause (to insert in Order Form):
"Billing entity & tax responsibility: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Agreement or Master Services Agreement ("MSA"), the parties agree that invoicing for the Services under this Order Form will be issued to and payable by Acme US, Inc. ("Billing Entity"). Acme US, Inc. shall be solely responsible for any taxes, duties, or withholdings arising from payments made hereunder. Customer shall provide Redwood with any tax residency certificates or other documentation reasonably requested by Redwood prior to Redwood's issuance of invoices to the Billing Entity."

We also recommend:
- Add a short sentence confirming which legal entity is signing the Order Form (signatory block) and ensure Procurement signs with the Billing Entity if that's their requirement.
- If Finance wants Net45, require a signed PO number or credit approval as Lauren suggested.
- Ask Acme to confirm the exact legal name / EIN and provide a signed AP contact.

If you want, I can prepare a clean Order Form with the clause above and a parallel MSA annotation indicating the billing entity is for invoicing only. Once we have Acme's PO and tax docs, legal can finalize and route DocuSign.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
